security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU writes a faulting virtual address to stval (or vstval/htval) for a breakpoint exception triggered by a debug trigger type that is NOT defined by the RISC-V debug spec to provide an address to stval. The old spec text unconditionally required stval to be written for all breakpoint exceptions except ebreak/c.ebreak; the clarified text restricts stval writes to only those breakpoint exception types where the privileged/debug architecture explicitly defines that an address shall be written. If QEMU's trigger implementation (e.g. mcontrol6 with execute match, icount, itrigger, etrigger) unconditionally populates stval with a virtual address for every breakpoint exception regardless of trigger type, it violates this clarified normative requirement.
security_spec.summary: Sstvala narrowed: stval must only be written for breakpoint exceptions whose trigger type is defined to provide an address — unconditionally writing stval for all non-ebreak breakpoints is now a spec violation that leaks potentially uninitialized or incorrectly-scoped virtual addresses to supervisor/hypervisor mode
